clue.text: Like Van Gogh, for instance — messed up, with one ear

indicators.note: messed up in the surface; here messed alone says the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumble
taken as written, the rest of the jumble

explanation.surface: A nod to Van Gogh, the painter who famously ended up with only one ear after a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' looks like one phrase about the painter's state, but 'messed' is the jumbling signal and 'up' is part of what gets jumbled, along with ONE EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Gogh was Dutch, and the Netherlands is in Europe, so he is an example of a person from that continent.

clue.text: Attentive female occupying stage is happy

indicators.note: the answer occupies, or sits inside, the run of words stage is happy

explanation.surface: A woman who pays close attention, happily performing on a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese hostess trained to attend to and entertain guests.

clue.text: Servant who doesn't let things go 13 8?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-standing household servant
second meaning: one who keeps hold of things, rather than letting them go in one ear and out the other

explanation.walkthrough: 13 8 is the long answer IN ONE EAR AND OUT THE OTHER; someone who keeps what they hear is literally one who retains.
explanation.definitionFit: A household retainer is a servant of long standing; read as one word built from retain, it is also a person who holds on.

clue.text: Know how to put in anagram of ear in cryptic

indicators.note: put in says the next piece is placed inside the rearranged letters
anagram of openly asks for the letters of ear to be rearranged

parts.note: to know how to do something is to be able to, so can

explanation.surface: Reads like a setter's instructions on how to slip an anagram of ear into a cryptic clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to describe clue-writing itself; 'cryptic' at the end is the definition, not a comment on the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious or secret, much as cryptic means hidden or obscure in meaning.

clue.text: Fear, being tone-deaf etc, some instruments or others

definitions.note: plural noun: other instruments besides the lutes

indicators.note: someone tone-deaf has no ear for music, so the word Fear loses its ear

parts.note: taken as written, then losing EAR
lutes are stringed instruments

explanation.surface: A tone-deaf player fearing some instruments, or perhaps others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being tone-deaf' means having no ear, so FEAR drops EAR to leave F; add LUTES, and the result names other instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Flutes are woodwind instruments, so they are some others alongside the stringed lutes.

clue.text: Composed, having prepared in advance without hearing organ

indicators.note: without says the organ is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: forewarned is forearmed: forearmed means ready beforehand
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone calm and composed because they prepared beforehand, despite being deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed and composed both mean made up or put together, as a group is formed or composed of members.

clue.text: Discovered a bit of corn planted in line, not cut

indicators.note: planted in says the corn piece is set inside the other letters, like a seed
cut says the word not loses a letter from its middle

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its O
an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: Finding out that some corn was planted in a row and left uncut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not, cut' reads as uncut corn, but 'cut' trims the word not itself, losing its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Learnt in the sense of found out: to learn a fact is to discover it.

clue.text: Hear about breakfast or lunch, or possibly tea? It's a deal

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

parts.words: breakfast or lunch, or possibly tea
parts.note: all three can be verbs meaning to take a meal, so eat

explanation.surface: Discussing which meal to have and settling it with an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The meals look like nouns but each works as a verb: to breakfast, to lunch, to tea all mean to eat. TRY, as a court hears a case, goes about EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, a negotiated deal.

clue.text: See 13
Particular kinds of speech — ear got some, but only some

indicators.note: but only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's ear picks up a few special ways of talking, but only a few.
explanation.definitionFit: An argot is the private jargon or slang of a particular group, such as thieves.

clue.text: A point going in one (non-English) ear's garbled, inadvertently

indicators.note: going in says A and the point are placed inside the other letters

parts.note: un is French for one, so one in a language other than English

indicators.note: garbled says the letters of ear's are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written: EARS
W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Something said in someone's ear came out garbled, catching them off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: '(non-English)' tells you to say one in French; 'point' is a compass point, not a dot or tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Unawares is an adverb meaning without noticing or by surprise, so done inadvertently.

clue.text: At this point, use your ears, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the answer is spelt differently from the word spoken

parts.note: to use your ears is to hear

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen now, at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Here is an adverb meaning in this place or at this stage of things.

clue.text: Finished in a triple time tempo, finally dealt with

indicators.note: in says the finished piece sits inside the other letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, here three times over
finished means ended

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter

parts.note: the word whose end is taken

explanation.surface: A musical piece in triple time, its tempo finally sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'triple time' sounds like a waltz rhythm, but it is the abbreviation for time three times over.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to a task is to deal with it, so attended to means handled or seen to.

clue.text: Entering and leaving canals? Not 12 or 24

definitions.meaning: first meaning: passing straight through the ear canals, as sound ignored does
second meaning: not attended to or heeded, the answers at 12 and 24

explanation.walkthrough: The canals are ear canals, not waterways; words that go in one ear and out the other are not attended to or heeded, the answers at 12 and 24.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes advice that is heard but immediately forgotten or ignored by the listener.

clue.text: Recounts how ears could be disturbed with rant

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of their order, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing how a tirade could upset the listener's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate a story is to tell or recount it in order.

clue.text: Becoming aware of, in a form of cognition, once nothing's omitted

indicators.note: a form of says the letters of cognition are reshaped
omitted says one letter of the fodder is left out of the rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Awareness as a type of cognition once nothing has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: COGNITION has two Os; drop one and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing something is perceiving it or becoming conscious of it.

clue.text: Comb what protrudes from head in school

indicators.note: in says the head's protrusion sits inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: an ear sticks out from the side of the head

explanation.surface: A child combing something sticking out of their head at school, like lice-checking.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as with a fine-toothed comb.

clue.text: That woman's rising musical ability makes us listen again

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: her is that woman's, possessive
to have an ear for music is to have musical ability

explanation.surface: A woman's growing talent as a musician makes people want to hear her again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehear something, especially a legal case, is to hear it a second time.

clue.text: Uses what's between ears, has fun with left to right shift

indicators.note: shift says one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: to celebrate is to have fun, party

explanation.surface: A political shift from left to right, made by someone enjoying themselves and thinking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To cerebrate is to think, using the brain, which sits between the ears.

clue.text: One that hears about eg Joan of Arc in French festival

indicators.note: about means the hearing organ is wrapped around the saint

parts.note: the ear is the organ that hears

parts.words: eg Joan of Arc in French
parts.note: Joan of Arc is a female saint, Sainte in French, abbreviated Ste

explanation.surface: Someone listening to a talk on Joan of Arc during a French festival.
explanation.walkthrough: A female saint in French is Sainte, shortened to STE, not the English ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus.

clue.text: Piece from austere orchestra in enhanced sound system

indicators.note: Piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a stern orchestra's music played on a high-quality audio system.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in' into the definition; it is a link word joining wordplay to definition, since a stereo is an enhanced sound system, not 'in' one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo sound uses two channels for a fuller effect than mono, an improved audio set-up.

clue.text: Visibly less happy lacking attention — hence row

indicators.note: lacking says the attention is taken away

parts.note: tearier: closer to crying
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A child getting tearful when ignored, leading to an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel to fit the tears, but it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows placed one above another, as in a stadium.

clue.text: Note echoed later, splitting ears in disturbed city

parts.note: B is a note in the musical scale

indicators.note: splitting says the repeated note goes into the middle of the jumble
disturbed letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the same note B, repeated further on

explanation.surface: A note repeated so loudly that it splits the ears of people in an unsettled city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'echoed later' means the same note B turns up a second time, further along, where it splits the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the capital city of Queensland, Australia.

clue.text: End of list that guy had permanently fixed in memory, metaphorically

parts.note: etc, et cetera, is written at the end of a list
he'd is short for he had

explanation.surface: The last item on a list was something a man remembered forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something etched on the mind is engraved there, as if cut into metal, so not forgotten.

clue.text: Lacking lead, the editors considered

indicators.note: lacking its lead means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, so two of them

explanation.surface: Without a leader, the editorial team weighed things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed advice is to take notice of it and give it consideration.

clue.text: Note from one kind of singer heard

indicators.note: heard says the answer sounds like the singer

parts.note: a tenor is a high male singing voice

explanation.surface: A note sung by a tenor being heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Note looks musical but is a banknote: a tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is slang for a ten-pound banknote or ten-dollar bill.
